explain.say: Imagine you made a little game where a cat should walk to a fish. You press go, and the cat walks the wrong way! Do not worry: that mistake is called a bug, and fixing it is called debugging. Every coder does it. Look at the circle on the board.

faq.q: What is a bug in a program?
faq.a: A bug is a mistake in a program that makes it do something you did not want, like a character walking the wrong way or a score that never goes up.
asks: What does bug mean in coding?
What is an error in code?

faq.q: How do I find a bug?
faq.a: Run the program and watch what really happens. Then read the steps one by one, comparing each with what the program did, until you find the step that does the wrong thing.
asks: Tips for finding mistakes in code

faq.q: Why test again after a fix?
faq.a: To check the fix really worked and did not break something else. Testing again is the only way to be sure.

faq.q: Why is it called a bug?
faq.a: Engineers used the word bug for faults long before computers. In 1947 a team working with Grace Hopper found a real moth trapped in the Harvard Mark II computer and taped it in the logbook as the first actual case of a bug being found.
asks: Who found the first computer bug?
Was there a real bug in a computer?

faq.q: Is it bad to have bugs?
faq.a: No, everyone makes them, even expert programmers at big companies. Finding and fixing bugs is a normal part of coding and a great way to learn.
asks: Am I bad at coding if I have bugs?

facts: On 9 September 1947 operators of the Harvard Mark II computer taped a moth into their logbook, noting the first actual case of bug being found.
The word bug for a fault in a machine was used by engineers, including Thomas Edison, in the 1800s.

quiz.show: The smartest way to fix a bug is…
quiz.why: Changing one thing at a time shows you exactly which change fixed the bug.

wrong.0: If you change everything you will not know which change worked, and you may add new bugs.
wrong.2: Most of the program is probably fine; just find the wrong step.
